key_insight: Generative AI can produce multiple plausible turbulent-flow solutions, but physical fidelity requires validation beyond visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectra.
engineering_relevance: Potential engineering applications include stochastic closures, flow super-resolution, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification when observations or resolved scales are incomplete.
method: Reviews diffusion, score-based, and related probability-transport methods for turbulence.
Examines flow generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, and temporal evolution.
Proposes physics-aware validation and an open, standardized benchmark ecosystem.
evidence_signal: The abstract outlines evaluation priorities—including energy transfer, intermittency, conservation, temporal consistency, and ensemble diversity—rather than reporting quantitative model performance.
watch_item: Limited data, weak baselines, and incomplete physical validation may undermine claims of generalization and reproducibility.
paper_title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
